title: How honest are you
paragraphs: Let‘s be honest — I’m sure we‘ve all done something a little dishonest in our lives — maybe copying someone’s work, borrowing some money from a friend and not paying them back or being given too much change in a shop and keeping quiet about it. Or maybe I‘m wrong, maybe you’re a good, upstanding citizen who believes that honesty is the best policy.

This proverb, ‘honesty is the best policy‘, was written back in the 1700s by American statesman, Benjamin Franklin. We may agree that owning up to our mistakes and behaving in a genuine and decent way, is the right way to lead our lives. But is there something in our human nature that makes us unscrupulous? For example, in some shops and car parks you can find an honesty box — a box where you pay for something by putting money in it — but it relies on you putting the right amount of cash in. This relies on people being honest and not trying to cheat but it does provide a temptation to get away with not paying the full amount.

Philip Graves, a psychologist, and author of the book Consumerology, suggests that this temptation is part of our evolution. He says: “We have evolved with the capacity to be dishonest. It‘s part of our evolutionary psychological make up — because if we gain an advantage over the people around us, we have a greater chance of surviving.”

So why do we place such importance on being honest if we benefit from being dishonest? It’s because it is selfish behaviour — which other members of our social group won‘t like. If everybody acted selfishly and dishonestly all the time, the world would be a very unpleasant place. As Philip Graves says: “There is a balance to strike between the extent to which we can feather our own nest, so to speak, and the risk of being ostracised by the group.” So, for societies to work together we need to trust each other and therefore we need to be honest.

Being trustworthy with money is of course crucial for an economy to survive and there are laws to protect us from dishonest practices like corruption and fraud. But being honest with words is another matter; saying what we think to someone can get us into hot water. However a new anonymous messaging app has been designed that lets anyone with a link to your profile to send you a message without knowing who it’s from. The app now has 300 million users which perhaps indicates how honest we really like to be — but in all honesty, do you want to know what people think about you? Is honesty always the best policy?!

vocabulary.entry: dishonest [adj.] /dɪsˈɒnɪst/ 不诚实的；不老实的
vocabulary.example: It was dishonest of him to lie about his qualifications.
vocabulary.translation: 他谎报自己的资历是不诚实的。

vocabulary.entry: copying [n.] /ˈkɒpiɪŋ/ 抄袭；复制
vocabulary.example: Copying someone else‘s work is a form of cheating.
vocabulary.translation: 抄袭别人的作品是一种作弊行为。

vocabulary.entry: upstanding [adj.] /ʌpˈstændɪŋ/ 正直的；诚实的 (书面语)
vocabulary.example: He is an upstanding member of the community.
vocabulary.translation: 他是社区里一位正直的成员。

vocabulary.entry: owning up to [phr.] /ˈəʊnɪŋ ʌp tuː/ 承认；坦白 (口语)
vocabulary.example: He finally owned up to breaking the window.
vocabulary.translation: 他终于承认打碎了窗户。

vocabulary.entry: genuine [adj.] /ˈdʒenjuɪn/ 真诚的；真正的
vocabulary.example: She showed genuine concern for my problem.
vocabulary.translation: 她对我遇到的问题表现出真诚的关心。

vocabulary.entry: decent [adj.] /ˈdiːsnt/ 正直的；正派的
vocabulary.example: He‘s a decent man who always tells the truth.
vocabulary.translation: 他是个正直的人，总是说实话。

vocabulary.entry: unscrupulous [adj.] /ʌnˈskruːpjələs/ 肆无忌惮的；不择手段的 (书面语)
vocabulary.example: The unscrupulous salesman cheated his customers.
vocabulary.translation: 那个肆无忌惮的销售员欺骗了顾客。

vocabulary.entry: temptation [n.] /tempˈteɪʃən/ 诱惑；引诱
vocabulary.example: He resisted the temptation to eat the whole cake.
vocabulary.translation: 他抵抗住了吃掉整个蛋糕的诱惑。

vocabulary.entry: selfish [adj.] /ˈselfɪʃ/ 自私的；利己的
vocabulary.example: It was selfish of him to take the last piece of cake.
vocabulary.translation: 他拿走最后一块蛋糕是自私的。

vocabulary.entry: selfishly [adv.] /ˈselfɪʃli/ 自私地
vocabulary.example: He acted selfishly and didn‘t care about others.
vocabulary.translation: 他行为自私，不在乎别人。

vocabulary.entry: feather our own nest [phr.] /ˈfeðər ˈaʊər əʊn nest/ 中饱私囊；营私舞弊 (书面语)
vocabulary.example: The corrupt officials were caught feathering their own nests.
vocabulary.translation: 那些腐败官员被抓获中饱私囊。

vocabulary.entry: ostracised [adj.] /ˈɒstrəsaɪzd/ 被排斥的；被排挤的 (书面语)
vocabulary.example: He felt ostracised by his colleagues after the argument.
vocabulary.translation: 争吵后他感觉被同事们排挤了。

vocabulary.entry: trustworthy [adj.] /ˈtrʌstwɜːði/ 值得信赖的；可靠的
vocabulary.example: She is a trustworthy friend who never breaks a promise.
vocabulary.translation: 她是一个值得信赖的朋友，从不食言。

vocabulary.entry: hot water [n.] /hɒt ˈwɔːtə/ 麻烦；困境 (口语)
vocabulary.example: He got into hot water for being late again.
vocabulary.translation: 他因为再次迟到而陷入了麻烦。

vocabulary.entry: anonymous [adj.] /əˈnɒnɪməs/ 匿名的；无名的
vocabulary.example: The donation was made by an anonymous donor.
vocabulary.translation: 这笔捐款来自一位匿名捐赠者。

vocabulary.entry: profile [n.] /ˈprəʊfaɪl/ 个人资料；简介
vocabulary.example: You can update your profile on the website.
vocabulary.translation: 你可以在网站上更新你的个人资料。

vocabulary.entry: corruption [n.] /kəˈrʌpʃən/ 腐败；贪污 (书面语)
vocabulary.example: The government is fighting corruption.
vocabulary.translation: 政府正在打击腐败。

vocabulary.entry: fraud [n.] /frɔːd/ 欺诈；诈骗 (法律术语)
vocabulary.example: He was found guilty of fraud.
vocabulary.translation: 他被判犯有欺诈罪。

vocabulary.entry: proverb [n.] /ˈprɒvɜːb/ 谚语；格言
vocabulary.example: As the proverb goes, “Honesty is the best policy.”
vocabulary.translation: 正如谚语所说：“诚实为上策。”

vocabulary.entry: evolution [n.] /ˌiːvəˈluːʃən/ 进化；演变 (科学术语)
vocabulary.example: The theory of evolution explains how species change over time.
vocabulary.translation: 进化论解释了物种如何随时间变化。

sentences.english: Let‘s be honest — I’m sure we‘ve all done something a little dishonest in our lives — maybe copying someone’s work, borrowing some money from a friend and not paying them back or being given too much change in a shop and keeping quiet about it.
sentences.chinese: 老实说——我敢肯定我们在生活中都做过一些有点不诚实的事情——也许是抄袭别人的作业，向朋友借了钱却不还，或者在商店里收到多找的零钱却默不作声。

sentences.english: Or maybe I‘m wrong, maybe you’re a good, upstanding citizen who believes that honesty is the best policy.
sentences.chinese: 又或许我错了，也许你是一个优秀、正直的公民，相信诚实才是最好的处事原则。

sentences.english: This proverb, ‘honesty is the best policy‘, was written back in the 1700s by American statesman, Benjamin Franklin.
sentences.chinese: “诚实才是上策”这句谚语是美国政治家本杰明·富兰克林在18世纪写的。

sentences.english: We may agree that owning up to our mistakes and behaving in a genuine and decent way, is the right way to lead our lives.
sentences.chinese: 我们可能都认同，承认自己的错误，以真诚的和正直的方式行事，才是正确的生活方式。

sentences.english: But is there something in our human nature that makes us unscrupulous?
sentences.chinese: 但我们的人性中是否存在一些东西让我们变得肆无忌惮呢？

sentences.english: For example, in some shops and car parks you can find an honesty box — a box where you pay for something by putting money in it — but it relies on you putting the right amount of cash in.
sentences.chinese: 例如，在一些商店和停车场，你会看到一个诚信箱——一个你通过往里面放钱来支付东西费用的箱子——但这依赖于你放入正确数额的现金。

sentences.english: This relies on people being honest and not trying to cheat but it does provide a temptation to get away with not paying the full amount.
sentences.chinese: 这依赖于人们的诚实，不试图欺骗，但这确实提供了一种诱惑，让人有可能不付全款就蒙混过关。

sentences.english: Philip Graves, a psychologist, and author of the book Consumerology, suggests that this temptation is part of our evolution.
sentences.chinese: 心理学家、《消费学》一书的作者菲利普·格雷夫斯认为，这种诱惑是我们进化的一部分。

sentences.english: He says: “We have evolved with the capacity to be dishonest.
sentences.chinese: 他说：“我们在进化过程中具备了不诚实的能力。

sentences.english: It‘s part of our evolutionary psychological make up — because if we gain an advantage over the people around us, we have a greater chance of surviving.”
sentences.chinese: 这是我们进化心理构成的一部分——因为如果我们比周围的人获得优势，我们就有更大的生存机会。”

sentences.english: So why do we place such importance on being honest if we benefit from being dishonest?
sentences.chinese: 那么，如果我们能从不诚实中获益，为什么我们还如此重视诚实呢？

sentences.english: It’s because it is selfish behaviour — which other members of our social group won‘t like.
sentences.chinese: 这是因为不诚实是一种自私的行为——我们社会群体中的其他成员不会喜欢这种行为。

sentences.english: If everybody acted selfishly and dishonestly all the time, the world would be a very unpleasant place.
sentences.chinese: 如果每个人一直都自私地、不诚实地行事，这个世界将会变得非常令人不快。

sentences.english: As Philip Graves says: “There is a balance to strike between the extent to which we can feather our own nest, so to speak, and the risk of being ostracised by the group.”
sentences.chinese: 正如菲利普·格雷夫斯所说：“可以这么说，在我们中饱私囊的程度和被群体排斥的风险之间，需要找到一个平衡点。”

sentences.english: So, for societies to work together we need to trust each other and therefore we need to be honest.
sentences.chinese: 所以，为了让社会能够协同运转，我们需要相互信任，因此我们需要诚实。

sentences.english: Being trustworthy with money is of course crucial for an economy to survive and there are laws to protect us from dishonest practices like corruption and fraud.
sentences.chinese: 在金钱方面值得信赖对于经济的生存当然至关重要，而且有法律保护我们免受像贪污和欺诈这样不诚实的行为的侵害。

sentences.english: But being honest with words is another matter; saying what we think to someone can get us into hot water.
sentences.chinese: 但在言语上诚实则是另一回事；对别人说出我们的想法可能会让我们陷入麻烦。

sentences.english: However a new anonymous messaging app has been designed that lets anyone with a link to your profile to send you a message without knowing who it’s from.
sentences.chinese: 然而，一款新的匿名信息应用程序被设计出来了，它让任何有你个人资料链接的人都可以给你发信息，而你却不知道信息来自谁。

sentences.english: The app now has 300 million users which perhaps indicates how honest we really like to be — but in all honesty, do you want to know what people think about you?
sentences.chinese: 这款应用现在有3亿用户，这也许表明了我们到底有多希望自己诚实——但说实在的，你想知道人们是怎么看待你的吗？

sentences.english: Is honesty always the best policy?!
sentences.chinese: 诚实真的永远是上策吗？！
